resolutions.researcher_notes: Two independent primary sources confirm operating status. (1) 2021-08-29 single-source-procurement notice (广西信永工程咨询有限责任公司 via 采招网, archived as an image, archive.org item 2023-09-19-195825, HTTP 200; automated text screen FAILs because it is a screenshot image with no extractable text layer -- I downloaded the PNG and read it directly): states the 中缅管道钦州支线 (this pipeline) 'currently running at 6MPa' (目前运行压力为6MPa), i.e. actively conveying gas as of the notice date. (2) An archived CNPC/PipeChina Southwest Pipeline Branch facilities table (web.archive.org snapshot of cnpc.com.cn, HTTP 200 -- automated substring screen FAILs on this token too because the PDF's extracted text layer doesn't register a plain match, but I ran `pdftotext -layout` myself and the exact row is present) lists 中缅钦州支线 as an in-service facility of 西南管道分公司 commissioned 2014/7/6, i.e. long-operating with no indication of shutdown. Both false negatives are the documented url_verifier false-negative classes (image-only page; PDF text-extraction miss) -- content manually confirmed to support 'operating'.

Two independent sources confirm this is a natural-gas pipeline. (1) The CNPC facilities table (pdftotext-verified) lists 中缅钦州支线 under section header '三、天然气管道' (III. Natural Gas Pipelines), directly under CNPC's Southwest Pipeline Branch table -- unambiguous classification as gas, separate from the document's section I (crude oil) and II (refined products). (2) The 2021 procurement notice (read as image) states the branch runs '起自西二线南宁支干线的南宁末站' (originating from the West-East Gas Pipeline No.2 Nanning trunk-branch's Nanning terminal), i.e. it is a branch off a natural-gas trunk system, with volumetric throughput given in 万m³/d (cubic meters, the standard gas unit, not tons). Both confirm Fuel=Gas.

Single strong primary source: the CNPC/Southwest Pipeline Branch facilities table row for 中缅钦州支线 gives 投产时间 (commissioning date) 2014/7/6, matching recorded StartYear1=2014 exactly (verified via `pdftotext -layout`, which the automated verifier's substring screen missed -- documented PDF-extraction false negative). The 2021 procurement notice (my other source for this row) is a technical/relocation document and does not state a commissioning date, so this is a one-source confirmation -- tier medium, not high, though the source is authoritative (CNPC's own facilities register).

CNPC facilities table row for 中缅钦州支线 states 设计能力 (design capacity) = 14.4 亿方/年 = 1.44 bcm/y, an exact match to recorded Capacity=1.44/CapacityUnits=bcm/y (pdftotext-verified; automated substring screen false-negatived on this large PDF). Single source for this exact annual-capacity figure, so tier medium. Note for transparency, not a contradiction: the 2021 procurement notice separately states 'design throughput 700万m³/d' for the same branch -- a different technical parameter (a nameplate/peak daily flow figure for the relocation engineering scope) that does not correspond 1:1 to an annual-average capacity figure and is not being proposed as a competing Capacity value; only the CNPC table's matching annual figure is cited here.

Two independent sources give near-identical lengths for the same route (南宁末站 to 钦州港/广西石化炼厂末站): (1) 2021 procurement notice (read as image): '线路水平长约141.156km'; (2) CNPC facilities table (pdftotext-verified): 141.2 km. Both round to the recorded LengthKnown=141.00km within normal survey-vs-design rounding tolerance. High tier, independent sources (an engineering procurement notice vs. an internal corporate facilities register).

The 2021 procurement notice (read as image; automated text screen FAILs because it's a screenshot with no text layer) states '管径D813mm' for this exact branch (中缅管道钦州支线), an exact match to recorded Diameter=813/DiameterUnits=mm. The CNPC facilities table (my other source for this row) does not include a diameter column, so this is a single-source confirmation -- tier medium. This also resolves an initial suspicion (raised in the prior deep-sweep audit) that the 813mm value might be cross-contaminated from a different roster row (P4719, also 813mm) -- it is not; it is independently, directly sourced here for this specific segment.

Two independent sources confirm the Nanning->Qinzhou route. (1) 2021 procurement notice: '起自西二线南宁支干线的南宁末站，止于钦州港广西石化炼厂末站' (starts at the Nanning terminal station off the West-East Gas Pipeline No.2 Nanning branch, ends at the Qinzhou Port Guangxi Petrochemical refinery terminal station) -- confirms StartPrefecture=Nanning, EndPrefecture=Qinzhou, both Guangxi/China. (2) CNPC facilities table: row '中缅钦州支线, 西二线南宁站-钦州港站' (走向/位置 = route Nanning Station to Qinzhou Port Station), 途经省市 (province) = 广西 (Guangxi). Both independently corroborate start/end locations and province.

2 independent Chinese-language sources, not GEM-derived, not tracing to one wire story. china5e.com (中国能源网), 2019-10-09: reports the 闸口输气站至湛江输气站段 (Zhakou-to-Zhanjiang gas-station section, part of 粤西支线北海至茂名段 = the Beihai-Maoming branch) commissioned/put into service 2019-10-08 ('顺利投产'). gdzjdaily.com.cn (湛江云媒/Zhanjiang municipal media), 2022-08-09, via Wayback snapshot: reports the branch's full commercial operation beginning 2022-08-08 once it reached Maoming station ('粤西支线全面投入运营实现商业输气'). Together: a real, staged-into-service, currently operating gas transmission pipeline — supports Status=operating. VERIFIER NOTE: the live gdzjdaily.com.cn URL false-negatived on CJK substrings for a prior researcher (encoding issue); citing the Wayback snapshot (20250825132255) instead, which passes url_verifier cleanly.

Both sources explicitly describe this as a 天然气 (natural gas) transmission pipeline: china5e names the parent entity '中国石化天然气分公司' (Sinopec Natural Gas Company) operating the branch, fed by the Beihai LNG receiving terminal; gdzjdaily calls it '重要天然气能源通道' (an important natural-gas energy corridor) delivering gas to Zhanjiang-area gas utilities. Supports Fuel=Gas.

gdzjdaily.com.cn (2022-08-09), via Wayback snapshot: '8月8日，广西管道公司粤西支线茂名输气站开始向广东省管网连续平稳输气300万方，标志着粤西支线全面投入运营实现商业输气' — an EXACT match to StartYear1=2022/StartMonth1=8. Not listing china5e.com as a second ref here even though it's cited for Status/Fuel/Location: its 2019-10-08 date is for an earlier, different milestone (partial-segment commissioning of just 闸口-湛江, not the full branch reaching commercial operation), so it does not itself support the specific 2022-08 value — noting it only as background (the branch's genuine staged buildout culminating in the 2022-08 full-operation date this ref supports), not as corroboration of the date itself. Single strong source; tier=medium/independent=false.

gdzjdaily.com.cn: '广西管道粤西支线...年设计输气能力33亿方' (Yuexi/Beihai-Maoming branch annual design gas-transmission capacity: 3.3 billion m3) — an EXACT match to GEM's Capacity=3.30 bcm/y, specifically attributed to this branch. Single clean branch-specific figure; tier=medium/independent=false. NOTE ON A DIFFERENT FIGURE FOUND, NOT CITED: Sinopec's 2020-09 completion/environmental-acceptance report for the whole Guangxi LNG project (trqi.sinopec.com PDF, see Diameter unit below) lists '设计输量 40.5×10^8m3/a' (4.05 bcm/y) in its EIA-vs-actual comparison table for 粤西支线 — but the IDENTICAL '40.5' figure also appears in the same table's rows for the unrelated 主干线 (main trunk, 502km) and 柳州支线 (Liuzhou branch, 29km), i.e. it reads as a network/system-wide throughput design figure duplicated across every line-segment row rather than this branch's own exclusive capacity. Not used, to avoid citing a different metric under this branch's name.

DISAGREEMENT, not a dead end — flagging rather than citing per standing rule 2/'never propose refs for a different value'. GEM records LengthKnown=207.00km for this branch. THREE independent sources consistently give a different figure, all clustering ~203.6-204.5km, none near 207km: (1) gdzjdaily.com.cn 2022-08-09: '全长约204km'; (2) a 2020-07 tender bid document issued by 广西天然气管道有限责任公司 itself (bidcenter.com.cn via Wayback web.archive.org/web/20230927041543) itemizing '粤西支线段（闸口输气站-茂名末站）全长约204Km'; (3) Sinopec's official 2020-09 completion/environmental-protection-acceptance investigation report for the whole Guangxi LNG pipeline project (trqi.sinopec.com PDF, doc_20200928_527694089618.pdf) — its formal EIA-vs-actual comparison table gives 粤西支线（闸口输气站-茂名末站）as 204.53km at the environmental-review stage and 203.63km as actually built ('减少0.90km'), to 2 decimal places. All three sources are independent of each other (municipal media, a construction tender, and Sinopec's own regulatory acceptance filing) and all disagree with GEM's 207.00km by a consistent ~1.2-1.7km (the acceptance-report figure being the most precise and authoritative of the three, and itself ~3.4km short of 207.00). This reads as a genuine Length correction candidate (~203.6-204.5km) for a separate Update pass, not a ref-sweep fill — not citing any of the three as support for the recorded 207.00km value.

Both an EXACT match to GEM's Diameter=559mm. VERIFIER NOTE (LARGE PDF false-negative, per url_verifier's own documented caveat): the Sinopec PDF is ~42MB/~200+ pages; url_verifier returns 200 but 'missing expected' on '闸口输气站' because its extractor does not reach the whole document. Cannot cleanly support this compound value as recorded, per the no-different-value rule. StartLocation='Zhakou Transmission Station'/Beihai/Guangxi and EndLocation='Maoming Transmission Station'/Maoming district are now strongly corroborated by TWO independent, first-party-quality sources beyond what the prior deep-sweep audit had: Sinopec's 2020-09 completion/acceptance report states verbatim '粤西支线（闸口输气站-茂名末站）：粤西支线起始于北海市合浦县的闸口输气站，先后经过北海、玉林、湛江和茂名，终止于茂名末站' (starts at Zhakou Transmission Station in Hepu County/Beihai, terminates at Maoming terminal), and china5e.com independently corroborates the same 闸口(Zhakou)->茂名(Maoming) framing. (Same large-PDF verifier false-negative as the Diameter unit — manually confirmed via pdftotext, 84 hits.) BUT EndState/Province is recorded as 'Guangxi', which is wrong — Maoming (茂名市) is a Guangdong-administered prefecture-level city, not Guangxi (this is the SAME attribution bug already flagged by this row's deep-sweep validity leg, rows/P4715.json, recommending EndState/Province -> 'Guangdong'; gdzjdaily's own framing of the branch as connecting '广西和广东...横穿湛江市' is consistent with that). Per task instructions, a disagreement found on any field within the unit routes the whole unit to UNRESOLVED rather than a partial ref; this is a data-fix candidate for the Update workflow (already on record), not a ref-sweep fill. Station-name/city corroboration itself is solid and available (see sources above) whenever the province field gets corrected and a fresh ref request is issued for it.

Current_ref was empty; the only candidate citation for this row (gas.in-en.com/html/gas-3040179.shtml, footnote [16] on the gem.wiki page) fails live (403). Fetched its web.archive.org snapshot (20240528154925) instead of retrying the geo/rate-blocked origin: it loads fine (200) but its full text is entirely about a DIFFERENT, unrelated approval -- the Fusui-Chongzuo branch (扶绥-崇左天然气支线管道工程) -- with zero occurrences of 贵港 (Guigang) or 玉林 (Yulin) anywhere in the page. So even the archived original never supported this row; it was mis-cited from the start. The gem.wiki page's 'Status: Cancelled' tag for this entry itself carries no footnote in the raw markup (per the deep-sweep audit shard for this PID) -- it is an unsourced editorial call. I searched (贵港-玉林 天然气支线管道 项目核准; 玉林支线 贵港 天然气管道 取消) and the deep-sweep audit shard for this same PID independently ran equivalent Chinese queries -- neither turned up any approval notice, EIA, or news article naming a single Guigang-to-Yulin gas line, cancelled or otherwise. The one plausible primary source that plausibly seeded the wiki entry (2011 ifeng EIA, see Location unit) describes two separate spurs, neither of which is a 'Guigang-Yulin' line, so there is no independent basis to confirm OR refute 'cancelled' for the segment as currently named. Leaving UNRESOLVED rather than citing a source that (a) doesn't verify live at its origin and (b) doesn't actually discuss this segment even in its archived form.

Live (200), Chinese-language 2011-12-01 EIA notice titled '广西液化天然气（LNG）项目环境影响评价' (Guangxi LNG Project Environmental Impact Assessment) on 广西新闻网/ifeng.com, describing the whole Guangxi Beihai-LNG-terminal transport network (this row's own parent name is literally 'Guangxi LNG Terminal Transport Pipeline' / zh 广西北海LNG外输管道) as a natural-gas (天然气) transmission network with a 684.17 km main trunk plus branch spurs including one to Yulin (玉林支线) and one to Guigang (贵港支线). This confirms Fuel=Gas for the network this row belongs to. Only single-sourced (tier medium, not high) because -- per the Location/Status units below -- this specific row's exact route identity ('Guigang-Yulin' as one combined segment) does not clearly match either the Yulin spur or the Guigang spur described in this or any other source found, so I did not chase a second source narrowly matched to this exact segment name; the fuel-type finding rests on the parent network being unambiguously a natural-gas (not oil/NGL) project.

DISAGREEMENT, not a gap -- per task rules, not proposing this as support. The recorded value is one combined segment from Guigang to Yulin (StartPrefecture=Guigang, EndPrefecture=Yulin). The only primary source that plausibly underlies the wiki entry -- the 2011-12-01 ifeng.com EIA (live, 200, contains '贵港' and '137.7') -- instead documents TWO SEPARATE, non-contiguous spurs off the shared 684.17 km Beihai-Hechi trunk: (1) 玉林支线 (Yulin Branch), 137.7 km, routed Beihai->Yulin ('先后经过北海、玉林2个地市'), and (2) 贵港支线 (Guigang Branch), 50.0 km, routed Nanning->Guigang ('先后经过南宁、贵港2个地市'). Guigang and Yulin are the far endpoints of two different branches off the trunk in this source, not two ends of one 'Guigang-Yulin' pipeline -- so this source does not support the recorded combined Location and I am not citing it as if it did. The other candidate citation (gas.in-en.com/html/gas-3040179.shtml, footnote [16]) is dead at origin (403) and its web.archive.org snapshot (20240528154925) is entirely about an unrelated branch (扶绥-崇左/Fusui-Chongzuo), with zero mentions of 贵港 or 玉林. I ran additional Chinese searches (贵港-玉林 天然气支线管道 项目核准; 玉林支线 贵港 天然气管道) and found no approval notice, EIA, or news article naming a single Guigang-to-Yulin route. This matches and reinforces the existence/attribution concern already logged in this PID's deep-sweep audit shard (rows/P4717.json) -- recommend that concern be resolved (is this row mislabeled Yulin Branch, mislabeled Guigang Branch, or a genuinely separate line with no source found yet?) before a Location ref is sought, since finding a ref for the wrong route would create a fabricated-support problem, not fix a gap.

Status inferred from context, not a literal label. (1) gx.chinanews.com.cn (2022-08-03, url_verifier PASSES live) describes 广西天然气管道有限责任公司 actively, presently supplying gas to named downstream Liuzhou retailers (柳州东城燃气, 柳州中燃) -- gas reaching Liuzhou-area users confirms an operating, in-service line into the Liuzhou/Liudong area. Cross-checked against the sheet: LengthKnown=141.00km (matches both 141.2/141.156), Diameter=813mm (matches source 2 exactly — this is NOT a data-entry contamination from the similarly-813mm-diameter Liuzhou-Guilin Branch/P4719 elsewhere in this roster, as I initially suspected when the gem.wiki page itself shows a blank Diameter field; it is independently, separately sourced), Capacity=1.44 bcm/y (matches source 1 exactly, 14.4 亿方/年), StartYear1=2014 (matches source 1's 2014/7/6 commissioning date), Status=operating (source 2's 'currently running at 6MPa' directly confirms active operation; source 1 lists it as an in-service Southwest Pipeline Branch facility), Owner/Operator='National Pipe Network Group Southwest Pipeline Co., Ltd.' (matches source 1's document title/issuing entity, the Southwest Pipeline Branch of PipeChina), and Start/End locations Nanning->Qinzhou (matches both sources' route description, source 2 further specifying the Qinzhou-end terminus as the Guangxi Petrochemical refinery station). CLASSIFICATION: correctly a natural-gas transmission branch (source 1's table section III, 天然气管道) fed off the West-East Gas Pipeline 2 Nanning station, not a gathering/distribution line. DUPLICATE check against the full 43-row Guangxi roster: no match — the other 813mm-diameter rows (P4719 Liuzhou-Guilin Branch, 155.7km/2.5bcm/y; P4694 Guangdong West, 156.12km/4.0bcm/y) are different routes/lengths/capacities, not this pipe. A web search also surfaced an unrelated, much shorter (12km, 4MPa) 'Qinzhou branch' of the China-Myanmar main line serving local town-gas distribution — that is a distinct, smaller facility from this 141km trunk branch and is not in this roster, so no double-count risk there either. Both url_verifier.py runs on these two URLs returned OK/200 (liveness); the automated substring/content screen registered a FAIL on both (expected: PDF binary text extraction and an image-only archive.org page respectively) — per the verifier's own documented false-negative classes, both pages were read in full manually (PDF text extracted via the file-reading tool; the archive.org screenshot viewed as an image) and their content demonstrably supports every value above, so both are cited as verified per-source rather than discarded on the automated screen.

resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, well-documented project. The cited EIA report (gdee.gd.gov.cn/attachment/0/393/393845/3008234.PDF, '粘西天然气主干管网茂名-阳江干线项目环境影响报告书', May 2020) directly names this exact segment. I downloaded the full 608-page scanned PDF (33MB) and confirmed verbatim: '线路全长 156.12km，管径 D813mm，设计压力 9.2Mpa' and '本工程设计输量 40×108m3/a' and '项目总投资额 308369.5 万元' and '已于 2019 年 8 月 15 日取得项目核准文件' — these exactly match GEM's Length=156.12km, Diameter=813mm, Pressure=9.2MPa, Capacity=4.0bcm/y (40×10^8 m3/a), SegmentCost=3,083,695,000 RMB, and ProposalYear/Month=2019/8. NOTE: the worklist's automated existing_ref_checks flagged Length/SegmentCost/ProposalYear as 'value not found' against this same PDF — that is a false negative (the checker's PDF-text extraction apparently didn't reach/parse the relevant late-document section); I independently verified all three are present verbatim, so the current refs are valid and do not need restaging. A second, fully independent source — Sohu/阳江观察 news, 2020-05-10, passes url_verifier cleanly — separately confirms length 156.12km, pressure 9.2MPa, the same start/end locations, and gives construction start as 2020-03-30 (exact match to GEM's ConstructionYear/Month=2020/3). A third independent source, the Guangdong provincial government portal republishing Nanfang Daily (archived, verifier-passed), dated 2021-09-29, confirms pipe-laying completion on 2021-09-28 (93 days ahead of schedule), capacity 40億m3/年 (4.0bcm/y) again, and the same route: '东起阳江市红丰镇，西至茂名市公馆镇' — gives length as a rounded '154公里' (vs the EIA's precise 156.12km; a 1.4% rounding variance, not material). CLASSIFICATION: correct — Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission both confirmed by every source ('天然气主干管网'/trunk gas network throughout); the EIA classifies it under China's 200km+ oil-and-gas trunk pipeline EIA category (combined with adjoining segments), consistent with a transmission trunk line, not a distribution/gathering line. DUPLICATE: none — checked against the full 43-PID Guangxi roster; every other roster entry is a genuine Guangxi-province pipeline (Nanning, Liuzhou, Guilin, Baise, Hepu, etc.) or Guangxi LNG-terminal transport line. P4694 is part of a wholly separate PipeChina Guangdong provincial network ('Guangdong West Gas Pipeline Network' / 粘西天然气主干管网) that happens to sit adjacent to Guangxi — no geometry or naming overlap with any Guangxi roster row. ATTRIBUTION (the actual defect): StartLocation='Gongguan Town, Maonan District' and StartPrefecture/District='Maoming' are both correct (confirmed verbatim in the EIA and Sohu texts: '茂名市茂南区公馆镇'), but StartState/Province is recorded as 'Guangxi' — Maoming is unambiguously a prefecture-level city of Guangdong Province; there is no 'Maoming' in Guangxi. Every one of the four independent sources checked (2020 EIA, 2020 Sohu, 2021 gd.gov.cn/Nanfang Daily, 2022 Maoming municipal government work report) places the entire pipeline inside Guangdong (Zhanjiang–Maoming–Yangjiang–Jiangmen corridor); the pipeline's own name ('粘西' = 'West Guangdong') confirms it. Likely origin of the error: the EIA PDF names the origin station '广西 LNG 茂名输气站' (using '广西'/Guangxi) in exactly one place, versus 63 other correct uses of '广东'/Guangdong elsewhere in the same 608-page document — almost certainly an OCR/typo for '粘西' or '广东'; separately, the 2021 completion article notes the pipeline's *western terminus interconnects with* a different Guangxi–Guangdong branch line ('西与广西管道粘桂支线互联') — an interconnection point, not this pipeline's location. Either artifact plausibly explains how 'Guangxi' entered GEM's StartState/Province field. This misattribution is likely also why this Guangdong pipeline was swept into the china-guangxi-gas batch scope in the first place.

resolutions.researcher_notes: GEM's own gem.wiki page for this shared network names this segment 'Guigang–Yulin Branch 玉林支线 (贵港-玉林)', Status=Cancelled, Length=137.7 km cited to footnote [16] (cite_note-:0-16, sheet's harvested URL https://gas.in-en.com/html/gas-3040179.shtml). Two independent problems: (1) that cited URL (an NDRC-style approval notice for the unrelated Fusui-Chongzuo branch, per its own link text) now 404s -- it is dead and, going by its own title, never actually supported this segment. (2) I went to the ONE source gem.wiki's editors plausibly built the 137.7 km figure from -- a Dec 2011 EIA article republished on ifeng.com (广西液化天然气（LNG）项目环境影响评价, 广西新闻网, 2011-12-01) -- verified live (200) and containing both '贵港' and '137.7'. That article lists the ORIGINAL 2011 Guangxi LNG terminal-transport network as one 684.17 km trunk (Beihai-Hechi) plus SIX separate named branches, each with its own length and route: 粤西支线 187.2 km (Beihai-Maoming via Yulin), 玉林支线 (Yulin Branch) 137.7 km explicitly routed Beihai->Yulin ('玉林支线先后经过北海、玉林2个地市'), 防城港支线 70.44 km, 桂林支线 172.37 km, 柳州支线 35.0 km, and a SEPARATE 贵港支线 (Guigang Branch) 50.0 km routed Nanning->Guigang ('贵港支线先后经过南宁、贵港2个地市'). Nowhere in this primary source is there a combined 'Guigang-Yulin' branch -- Guigang and Yulin are the endpoints of two DIFFERENT spurs off the main trunk, not two ends of one line. GEM's wiki entry appears to have grafted the Yulin Branch's length (137.7 km) onto a name/endpoint pair ('Guigang-Yulin') that matches neither the Yulin Branch (Beihai->Yulin) nor the Guigang Branch (Nanning->Guigang) as documented in 2011. On the actual GEM sheet itself the row carries no Length/Diameter/Capacity at all (worklist shows only Status/Fuel/Location units, all MISSING_REF) -- so the sheet doesn't inherit the wiki's mismatched number, but the Location value (StartPrefecture=Guigang, EndPrefecture=Yulin) does inherit the questionable naming. I searched independently in Chinese (贵港-玉林 天然气管道; 贵玉支线 天然气管道; 广西天然气支线管网 贵港 玉林 项目核准) and found no approval notice, news article, or EIA that names a single Guigang-to-Yulin gas transmission line, cancelled or otherwise. Given (a) the row's only traceable citation is dead/mismatched, (b) the one plausible source it could derive from actually describes two different, non-contiguous spurs, and (c) no independent source names this combined route at all, I'm flagging this as an existence/attribution concern rather than accepting it as a distinct confirmed project. This is NOT a call that the underlying network/branches don't exist -- the 2011 EIA is solid, live evidence that Guangxi's LNG-terminal transport network did plan both a Yulin-bound spur and a Guigang-bound spur -- it's a call that P4717 as currently named/located does not clearly correspond to either.

(1) The gem.wiki page's own 53-item reference list was read in full for leads (never cited): NOT ONE citation on the page mentions Liuzhou/Liudong/Luonan/Liunan (checked for every variant: 柳州, 柳南, 罗村, 柳东) — the page's citations are almost all for OTHER segments sharing this same wiki article (南宁-凭祥, 桂林-灵川-兴安, 河池-南丹, 来宾-武宣-象州-金秀, 梧州-峑溪, 南宁-崇左, etc.). A row whose only wiki support is a generic aggregate page that never names it is an existence flag by the brief's own rule, so I went straight to independent open-web search. (2) Found a Tier-1 independent confirmation: the PRC National Development and Reform Commission's official Dec-2023 cross-provincial gas pipeline tariff table (ndrc.gov.cn PDF, read directly — not via the lossy substring extractor) lists as its own line item #15: '广西LNG外输管线' (Guangxi LNG External Transmission Pipeline), start 广西北海 (Beihai), end 广西柳州 (Liuzhou), with named branches '柳东支线、粤西支线、桂林支线' (Liudong Branch, Yuexi/West-Guangdong Branch, Guilin Branch). '柳东支线' = Liudong Branch is an EXACT structural match to P4718's route (Liuzhou Transmission Station → Liudong Transmission Station) — this is real, officially tariffed infrastructure, not a phantom. (3) Second independent source: a Guangxi-bureau chinanews.com.cn article (2022-08-03, verified live + content-checked with a corrected UTF-8 decode after the verifier's default encoding auto-detect mis-flagged it as ISO-8859-1 — the raw bytes do contain 广西天然气管道有限责任公司, 柳州, 柳州东城燃气, 柳州中燃) confirms this same operator company actively supplies downstream Liuzhou gas retailers, and states the whole '广西LNG管道' network is now 735km through 7 cities. (4) DUPLICATE check against the roster: P4719 shares the identical start point (Liuzhou Transmission Station, Luoman Town, Liunan District) but is 155.7km/813mm vs P4718's 29km/610mm, and is very likely the network's separate, larger '桂林支线' (Guilin Branch, per the same NDRC list — corroborated by a 14th-Five-Year-Plan item accelerating a 'Guangxi LNG external pipeline Guilin branch (Liuzhou–Guilin)') — a genuinely different, longer, larger-diameter line to a different destination than P4718's short local spur into Liudong New Area (柳东新区), a well-known development district inside Liuzhou city itself. Different NDRC-named branches, different endpoints, different diameters — not a double-count. (5) CLASSIFICATION: Fuel=Gas is correct; this is a genuine natural-gas transmission branch, not a gathering/feeder line. CAVEAT (SPEC): could not independently confirm the exact 29km length, 610mm diameter, or 2013 StartYear1 for this specific branch in any open source — a single weak trade-press source (shiyouyuzhuangbei.com, 2016) states that natural-gas branch pipeline construction in '柳州' (among several named cities) began in 2015, which chronologically could not precede a 2013 in-service date IF it refers to the same segment; however the sentence names Liuzhou only as one of several general-purpose branch projects and does not specify which route, so this may describe a different Liuzhou-area line entirely. Flagging rather than silently passing it, per the standing rule, but not escalating to a hard 'concern' given the single-source ambiguity.

resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/SPEC: confirmed by 2 independent government/state-media sources naming this exact segment (Liuzhou-Guilin), not GEM-derived. (1) gx.chinanews.com.cn (2023-09-30, Guangxi Chinanews) reports the 'Guangxi LNG supporting export pipeline Guilin branch' (广西LNG配套外输管道桂林支线) ran Liuzhou Transmission Station (Luonan/Luoman Town) -> Guilin Transmission Station (Sitang Town), 155.7 km, 813 mm diameter, 10 MPa design pressure, Phase-1 capacity 2.5 bcm/y, completed an 8 MPa/72-hour trial run and was commissioned 2023-09-29 -- this matches GEM's Length (155.70 km), Diameter (813 mm), Pressure (10.00 MPa), Capacity (2.50 bcm/y), StartYear1/Month1 (2023-09) and Status=operating exactly. (Note: url_verifier flagged this URL as a false negative on '桂林'/'2.5' -- likely an encoding/rendering artifact in the automated fetch; a WebFetch read of the same URL returned the full matching figures verbatim, so I'm citing it.) (2) sasac.gov.cn (2019-12-25, State Council SASAC, sourced from Sinopec) reports the 'Guangxi pipeline Guilin branch' (广西管道桂林支线) broke ground 2019-12-17 in Liucheng County, Liuzhou, as part of the national 'south gas north' mid-corridor (Beihai-Liuzhou-Guilin-Hengyang-Qianjiang...), design length 165 km -- this matches GEM's ConstructionYear/Month (2019-12). The 165 km design figure vs. 155.7 km as-built figure is a normal pre-construction-estimate-vs-final gap (~5%), not a red flag; the as-built 155.7 km from the 2023 commissioning article is the correct current value and is already what's on the sheet. DUPLICATE CHECK vs roster: P4718 ('Liuzhou Branch') shares the identical StartLocation string ('Liuzhou Transmission Station, Luoman Town, Liunan District') but is a distinct, much shorter segment (29 km, 610 mm) running Liuzhou->Liudong Transmission Station -- a different physical spur off the same hub station, not the same pipe as this 155.7 km Liuzhou->Guilin trunk. Not a duplicate. FuelSource='Guangxi LNG Terminal' is consistent with both sources, which describe this branch as the outlet moving Beihai-LNG-sourced gas north. Net: this row's specific data (cancelled/2022/no length) looks unsupportable as recorded, and its true likely status (given the wiki-vs-EIA convergence on 70.44 km / operating) needs a proper Update pass rather than a rubber stamp. Separately, Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission both cite http://fgw.gxzf.gov.cn/zfxxgkzl/wjzx/xmpf/xiangmuhezhunpifu/t2198133.shtml, which times out on every attempt (ConnectTimeout via url_verifier, ECONNREFUSED via direct fetch) -- unverifiable right now, though both values are plausible defaults for this network and I am not flagging them as wrong, just unconfirmed.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Existence: solidly confirmed independent of GEM/wiki. The operating company is real and verifiable: cnstock.com (2024-06-13, verified) profiles '国家管网广西公司' (National Pipeline Network Guangxi Company) under the headline 'from one pipe to one network,' consistent with the wiki's own claim that the pipeline transferred to PipeChina in July 2020. ljzfin.com (verified, tokens '1318' and '2013' both present) independently confirms a Beihai LNG terminal external-transmission pipeline exists, gives construction start July 2013 (matches GEM StartYear1=2013) and trial operation March 2016, a design diameter of 800mm, and states the network totals 1,318 km across 18 stations/49 valve chambers reaching major Southwest China cities -- this is a materially different (much larger) total than GEM's 684 km, though it likely describes a broader distribution scope (trunk + downstream city branches) rather than one discrete segment, so it's a caveat rather than proof GEM is wrong. Classification (Fuel=Gas, a gas transmission trunk) is correct -- this is unambiguously the gas trunk delivering regasified LNG from the Beihai terminal, not a gathering/feeder line. Duplicate check against the roster: P4715/P4716/P4718/P4719/P4720/P4723 all share the identical pipeline_name 'Guangxi LNG Terminal Transport Pipeline' and are described on the SAME gem.wiki page as named sub-branches (Beihai-Maoming Branch=P4715 207km/3.3bcm/y match exact; Liuzhou-Guilin Branch=P4719 155.7km/2.5bcm/y match exact; Liuzhou Branch~27km=P4718 29km close match; a further 'Qinzhou-Fangchenggang' 70.44km branch mentioned on the page has no obvious matching PID in the 43-row roster and may be untracked). Given P4718 and P4719 both explicitly originate FROM 'Liuzhou Transmission Station' -- the same district/prefecture where P4721 (684km) TERMINATES -- the most likely topology is P4721 = the long-haul trunk arriving at Liuzhou, with P4718/P4719 as further downstream spurs from that arrival point, not parallel duplicates of the trunk's mileage. I therefore did NOT flag this as concern_type=duplicate, but a human should still eyeball the two pipelines' route geometry (once routed) to rule out overlap, especially given the unresolved 1,318km discrepancy above. Owner/Operator: Owner1 'Guangxi Natural Gas Pipeline Co Ltd' (100%) matches the QCCOwner Chinese name '广西天然气管道有限责任公司' and is consistent with independent sourcing; however a Baidu Baike lookup (NOT cited/used as a source per project standards -- crowd-sourced, unverifiable tier) surfaced an unconfirmed claim that this company's equity changed on 2025-08-11 to give PipeChina 100% direct control (implying it may not have been 100% PipeChina-owned before that date) -- this is an attribution lead worth someone chasing through an actual PipeChina/SASAC disclosure filing, not something I'm willing to act on from a wiki-tier source alone.

resolutions.segment_name: Beihai Tieshan Port loop gas pipe line
resolutions.recommendation: Keep the row, but replace the current [ref] on Status/Fuel/Capacity/Pressure/Length/Diameter/Location/SegmentCost (the fgw.gxzf.gov.cn generic 2023 work-plan notice) with a project-specific source such as the safety-evaluation registry entry below, which actually names this pipeline and its route.
resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: this pipeline is real and independently corroborated. It is the '广西天然气支线管网项目铁山港天然气支线管道工程' (Guangxi Natural Gas Branch Pipeline Network Project - Tieshan Port Natural Gas Branch Pipeline Project), built by 广西燃气集团有限公司 (Guangxi Gas Group Co., Ltd.). Independent, separately-run confirmation comes from (1) a Guangxi natural-resources-department land pre-approval registry entry (dnr.gxzf.gov.cn, approved 2024-04-02, project name matches verbatim, land area 2.5441 hectares) and (2) a safety-evaluation-industry disclosure registry (河南油田工程科技股份有限公司's public safety-evaluation-info platform, an entity unconnected to the Guangxi government) which independently names the same project, describes its route (starts at Sinopec's Guangxi Phase-III LNG receiving terminal outer wall, passes a #1 valve chamber / Tieshan Port first station / Nanzhuwan distribution station, ends at Xinggang distribution station) and gives a total pipe length of 3.14km (gas-source connector line) + 25.89km (south loop network) = ~29.0km, evaluated 2023-09 to 2023-12. A third source (an EIA-public-participation notice reprint, yanshougs.com, 2023-10-24) independently names the same project and builder. IMPORTANT SOURCING CAVEAT on GEM's OWN current ref: the cited fgw.gxzf.gov.cn URL (t16217273.shtml) IS a real, live page (confirmed via a 2025-04-13 Wayback snapshot after the live host itself was unreachable from this session), but it is titled '广西壮族自治区发展和改革委员会关于印发《广西能源基础设施建设2023年工作推进方案》的通知' - a generic annual energy-infrastructure work-plan ISSUANCE notice. Its visible body text never names Tieshan Port or this pipeline; any project-specific figures would only live in an attached investment-plan spreadsheet that is not retrievable standalone. This is exactly the 'generic/aggregate citation that does not actually name this pipeline' pattern the sweep is meant to catch - it happens the pipeline itself is real, but the cited ref does not actually support the values it is attached to. CLASSIFICATION: correctly recorded as gas transmission - this is a large-diameter (DN800/DN500 per the route description found), high-pressure branch trunk connecting an LNG import terminal to city-gate distribution stations, not a small gathering/distribution line. DISTINCT-PROJECT WARNING for future researchers: there is a SECOND, textually similar but functionally different pipeline in the same Tieshan Port area - '铁山东港天然气支线管道项目' (Tieshan 'East Port' gas branch pipeline project, serving the 东港产业园区/East Port Industrial Park), originally developed by 广西顺华公司/天圜能源公司 and acquired via a 2024-02-07 equity-transfer signing by Guangxi Energy Group's subsidiaries (广投管网公司, 广投北海燃气公司) - reported by a Chinese energy trade press article. As of that Feb-2024 report it was still awaiting 通气投产 (gas commissioning). This is NOT the same project as P7664 (different developer, different industrial-park framing) and does not appear to be in the 43-row Guangxi roster under any other PID - flagging as a discovery lead for the country's discovery workstream, not folding it into this row. DUPLICATE check against the full roster: no other row names Tieshan Port as start/end, so P7664 is not a relabel of an existing row.
